transcript.text: Good morning everyone. I've called this cross-functional check to finalize the production and shipment plan for the customer order of 3,600 pump modules — 600 sterile and 3,000 standard. As you know, Assembly Cell 2 is down due to an electrical fault, so we're working with Cells 1 and 4 only, and the customer requires shipment in the upcoming Sunday-Monday window. Before I lock the schedule, I need input from each of you: process engineering on cell capabilities and cycle times for both module types, quality systems on any inspection or validation requirements, workforce coordination on staffing availability across shifts, and logistics on pickup and loading constraints. Let's go around the table.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to flag two important constraints on Cell 4 that aren't in the schedule yet. My commissioning review this morning found that Cell 4's newly installed fixture requires exactly 2 hours of setup verification before it can be used, and Cell 4 is approved for no more than 1,200 modules during this campaign. The commissioning note hasn't been entered into the production schedule yet, so please factor these in before we lock anything.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical quality requirement from the customer control plan. I confirmed in the current customer control plan — the revised version I pulled from the customer portal yesterday — that all 600 sterile-pump modules must run exclusively on Cell 1 and receive a 100 percent pressure test before packing. This is because Cell 4 has no compatible pressure tester. I want to warn everyone that the local work-order file still shows the ordinary inspection route, so if anyone is working from that file, they will not see this requirement. All 600 sterile modules must go through Cell 1, not Cell 4.

transcript.text: I need to share my Sunday roster findings. I verified with supervisors this afternoon that the qualified staffing requirement is exactly 4 operators for Cell 1 and exactly 5 operators for Cell 4 — and those are the only qualified operators available for this order. I haven't attached this to Elena's draft schedule yet, so everyone should factor these staffing numbers in before we lock the plan.

transcript.text: I need to share my carrier confirmations before we lock the plan. I received email confirmations today reserving capacity for exactly 2,400 modules from Dock 2 by Sunday at 18:00 and exactly 1,200 modules from Dock 2 by Monday at 08:00. These appointments have not yet been copied into the shipment plan, so Elena's draft won't reflect them. This gives us two shipment windows: 2,400 modules by Sunday evening and the remaining 1,200 by Monday morning, all out of Dock 2.
